chapter_theme: A song at Thiruppazhaiyarai (திருப்பழையாறை): the poet, a slave to women he serves for love, asks Murugan to scold him like a mother and speak one word of teaching so he gains the feet; the praise names the hero of the sea-battle and the son of Siva who is half Uma, at the golden temple of Pazhaiyarai.

877.reading: The poet describes women whose eyes run to the ears like spears and whose camphor-scented breasts are like lotus buds, and calls himself a rubbish-minded slave and sinner who, caught by them, took up their service and ran after them with love; he asks Murugan to be angry with him like a mother and speak one word of teaching, so that by that grace he gains the feet. The praise names the playful, generous hero who sent the vel at Sura in the sea, the younger brother of the elephant-faced one, the son of Siva who dances with Uma as his half and wears the Vedas as his loincloth, at the golden temple of Pazhaiyarai with its towers and walls like mirrors.
877.nuance: கோபித்துத் தாயென நீ ஒரு போதத்தைப் பேச: the plea asks for a mother's scolding and a single teaching (போதம்), grace that corrects. ஊழியமே பற்றி: the poet's service has gone to women instead of to the Lord. வேதப் பொற் கோவண ஆடையர் gives Siva the Vedas as his loincloth. A few words (கூளச் சித்தாளன், மூளன்) are uncertain.
